title: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy: preeclampsia, severe features, eclampsia, HELLP syndrome and antihypertensive therapy
subject: ss-obg
refs: ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 222: Gestational Hypertension and Preeclampsia
ISSHP Classification, Diagnosis & Management of the Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy (2021)

steps.say: Preeclampsia arises from defective endovascular trophoblast remodeling of uterine spiral arterioles. Failure to transform these vessels into wide, low-resistance conduits leads to chronic placental ischemia, triggering the release of soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase-1 into maternal circulation.
steps.tx: The fundamental pathogenesis of **preeclampsia** involves failed second wave of **endovascular trophoblast invasion**, leaving maternal **spiral arterioles** narrow, stiff, and vasoactive. Chronic placental hypoxia provokes excess release of anti-angiogenic **soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase-1** (sFlt-1), inducing generalized maternal endothelial dysfunction and multiorgan injury.

steps.say: International guidelines define gestational hypertension and preeclampsia by strictly standardized diagnostic criteria. Blood pressure measuring 140 millimeters of mercury systolic or 90 diastolic on two occasions at least 4 hours apart after 20 weeks gestation establishes new-onset gestational hypertension.
steps.tx: Diagnosis of **gestational hypertension** requires **blood pressure** of 140 mmHg systolic or 90 mmHg diastolic or higher on 2 occasions at least 4 hours apart after 20 weeks of gestation. Coexisting **proteinuria** (>= 300 mg/24 hours or protein-creatinine ratio >= 0.3) confirms preeclampsia.

steps.say: Severe features of preeclampsia identify patients at immediate risk of cerebrovascular hemorrhage, pulmonary edema, or eclampsia. Critical criteria include persistent severe blood pressure of 160 over 110 or greater, thrombocytopenia below 100,000 per microliter, and serum creatinine exceeding 1.1 milligrams per deciliter.
steps.tx: Preeclampsia with **severe features** is established by systolic BP >= 160 or diastolic >= 110 mmHg, **thrombocytopenia** (platelet count < 100,000/microL), impaired liver transaminases (ALT/AST twice normal), renal insufficiency (**serum creatinine** > 1.1 mg/dL), pulmonary edema, or persistent cerebral disturbances.

nodes.label: Identify maternal BP >= 160/110 mmHg or severe symptoms
Obtain urgent platelet count, transaminases, and creatinine
Document severe features (platelets < 100k, Cr > 1.1, elevated enzymes)
Initiate seizure prophylaxis with MgSO4 and prepare delivery at 34 weeks

steps.say: Eclampsia manifests as new-onset generalized tonic-clonic seizures in a woman with preeclampsia, unrelated to other neurological disorders. Magnesium sulphate is the drug of choice for both preventing and treating eclamptic seizures, acting primarily through central NMDA receptor antagonism.
steps.tx: The clinical occurrence of generalized tonic-clonic seizures in preeclampsia constitutes **eclampsia**. **Magnesium sulphate** remains the undisputed gold standard anticonvulsant for seizure termination and prophylaxis, outperforming phenytoin and diazepam via central **NMDA receptor blockade**, cerebral arterial vasodilation, and blood-brain barrier protection against edema.

left.title: Zuspan Intravenous Regimen
points: Loading dose: 4 g IV over 15 to 20 minutes
Easier to titrate and less painful than IM

right.title: Pritchard Intramuscular Regimen
points: Loading: 4 g IV plus 10 g IM (5 g in each buttock)
Ideal in low-resource settings without infusion pumps

steps.say: Administering magnesium sulphate requires diligent clinical monitoring to detect hypermagnesaemia before toxicity develops. Clinical safety checks include confirming brisk patellar deep tendon reflexes, a respiratory rate of at least 12 breaths per minute, and hourly urine output exceeding 30 milliliters.
steps.tx: Safe administration of magnesium requires active **patellar reflex** monitoring, **respiratory rate** maintained above 12 breaths per minute, and **urine output** > 30 mL/hr. If toxicity emerges, intravenous **calcium gluconate** (1 g of 10% solution over 3 minutes) serves as the immediate antidote.

rows: Loss of deep patellar tendon reflexes
Withhold infusion and check renal function
Stop infusion and give IV calcium gluconate
Cardiac arrest and severe conduction block

steps.say: HELLP syndrome represents a severe variant of preeclampsia characterised by microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, elevated hepatic transaminases, and low platelets. Laboratory diagnosis requires characteristic fragmented schistocytes, serum LDH exceeding 600 units per liter, and severe thrombocytopenia.
steps.tx: The **HELLP syndrome** comprises microangiopathic **hemolytic anemia** with fragmented schistocytes, elevated liver transaminases (**serum LDH** > 600 U/L, AST/ALT >= 70 U/L), and profound **low platelet count** (< 100,000/microL). Both the Tennessee and Mississippi classification systems guide clinical risk stratification and prompt delivery planning.

steps.say: Acute severe hypertension requires urgent medical reduction to prevent maternal intracranial hemorrhage and aortic dissection. First-line parenteral antihypertensive agents include intravenous labetalol and intravenous hydralazine, alongside oral immediate-release nifedipine.
steps.tx: Acute treatment of severe pregnancy hypertension (BP >= 160/110 mmHg) prevents maternal stroke using intravenous **labetalol** (20 mg initially, doubling to 40 and 80 mg every 10 to 20 minutes) or intravenous **hydralazine** (5 to 10 mg), with oral **oral nifedipine** (10 to 20 mg capsule) as an effective alternative.

nodes.label: Administer IV labetalol 20 mg over 2 min (or IV hydralazine 5 mg)
Re-check BP at 10 to 20 minutes; escalate labetalol to 40 mg then 80 mg
Target BP 140 to 150 / 90 to 100 mmHg without compromising placental flow

steps.say: Definitive resolution of preeclampsia requires delivering the fetus and placenta. In women with preeclampsia with severe features, delivery is mandated at 34 weeks of gestation, whereas stable preeclampsia without severe features is safely managed until 37 weeks.
steps.tx: The definitive cure for preeclampsia is **delivery timing**. Pregnancies complicated by preeclampsia with severe features mandate delivery at **34 weeks** gestation (or earlier if HELLP, pulmonary edema, or eclampsia occur), whereas preeclampsia without severe features is managed expectantly until **37 weeks**.
